claims.claim: (b) #232's createRouteLoadMachine (src/lib/loading/routeLoad.ts) exposes exactly the seam the fix needs: a plain non-mutating generation getter and isCurrent(g), explicitly documented as the external co-guard idiom for page-owned reconciles that capture generation without bumping it and compare later.
claims.evidence: routeLoad.ts header comment: 'machine.generation / machine.isCurrent(g) are the EXTERNAL co-guard seam: #260's refreshCompletionGate and roster's several structural-write reconciles capture the generation WITHOUT bumping it, then compare later.' The same page already uses this exact idiom four times for section writes (const g = routeLoad.generation; ... if (g !== routeLoad.generation) return;) at lines 1047/1091/1095, 1487/1511, 1600/1644, 1786/1805/1809 — so the fix is 'use the established idiom at 3 more sites,' not new machinery.

claims.claim: (c) The finding is still reachable post-#232 exactly as described; the panel-reset path (isSwitch-gated clear of showInactive/inactiveRows/inactiveLoadError) was preserved from #255 into the new reset() callback, and none of the three sites were absorbed into the machine.
claims.evidence: reset callback in +page.svelte lines 113-124 clears the panel only 'if (isSwitch)', citing '#255 review r3 F2' verbatim and explaining the refresh-vs-switch distinction is unchanged. The template gates rendering on {#if showInactive} (line 3663) — a stale write while the panel is closed silently repopulates inactiveRows, then the NEXT toggleInactive open on the new collective flips showInactive=true synchronously while the old loadInactiveRoster await for that same reopen is still in flight, so stale rows render until it settles — matching the issue's repro shape verbatim. Unrelated to routeLoad internals except that all three sites read currentCfg/cfg, which routeLoad's own load() callback sets (line 146).

claims.claim: (d) page.roster-deactivate.spec.ts's '(B) inactive surface' describe block (lines 337-542) pins the panel behavior; its two closest tests ('switching collectives clears the panel', line 437; 'a deactivate with the panel OPEN refreshes the panel too', line 485) exercise the reset-on-switch and refresh-not-switch paths but NOT the actual race window (a switch landing while one of the three loadInactiveRoster awaits is still unresolved) — so a new guard test can be added without touching those two.
claims.evidence: The 'switching collectives clears the panel' test switches selectedCollectiveDbStore only after waitFor confirms the panel is already populated (post-settle), never during an in-flight loadInactiveRoster call. The 'deactivate refreshes panel' test never switches collectives at all (pure refresh). Neither leaves loadInactiveRoster's mock unresolved across a switch. A guard test needs: open panel (or trigger deactivate/reinstate) with loadInactiveRosterMock pending (unresolved promise), switch collective mid-flight, resolve the stale promise, assert its stale rows never land in inactiveRows/render under the new collective.

claims.claim: (e) The fix is still the ~3-lines-x-3-sites shape Bentham estimated in scale, but NOT a uniform 'capture routeLoad.generation at function entry' copy-paste across all three sites — handleDeactivateConfirm and handleReinstate call await loadForSelected() themselves (lines 801, 871) before their own loadInactiveRoster reload, and loadForSelected() unconditionally bumps routeLoad's generation counter even on a same-db refresh, so capturing g before that self-triggered call would make isCurrent(g) spuriously false on every ordinary (non-race) run.
claims.evidence: routeLoad.ts loadForSelected(): 'const g = ++generation;' runs unconditionally, before isSwitch is even computed and independent of it. In +page.svelte, handleDeactivateConfirm/handleReinstate each call await loadForSelected() (lines 801/871) THEN inactiveRows = await loadInactiveRoster(cfg) (lines 809/874) — so a naive const g = routeLoad.generation at the top of these two functions would already be stale by the time of the vulnerable await, always short-circuiting the legitimate write. Correct placement is to capture g AFTER the await loadForSelected() line in those two sites; toggleInactive has no such self-refresh call, so capturing at its function entry (before its single await) is correct as-is. All four existing routeLoad.generation precedent sites on this page (renameSection/removeSection/reorder/reparent handlers) never call loadForSelected() themselves, so none of them hit this nuance — it is specific to these two lifecycle handlers and not covered by rote pattern-matching the existing idiom.

risks: Capturing g at the wrong point in handleDeactivateConfirm/handleReinstate (top-of-function instead of right after their own await loadForSelected()) would silently break the normal case: isCurrent(g) would read false on every deactivate/reinstate with the panel open, even with no collective switch, so the inactiveRows reload would be skipped and the panel would go stale after every ordinary deactivate/reinstate. This is easy to get wrong by pattern-matching the four existing routeLoad.generation sites without noticing they don't call loadForSelected() themselves.

The new guard test needs an unresolved-promise mock (release-controlled, like the existing 'second tap while reinstate in flight' test at line 403 already does for reinstateMemberMock) combined with a mid-flight collective switch — no existing test in the file does both together, so this is genuinely new test infrastructure, not a copy of an existing case.

Not verified in this pass: whether fix-255/merge-255 (agents listed as active in this session) have already started work on this issue — worth a SendMessage check before dispatching, to avoid duplicate work on the same three sites.
